threatModel.summary:
Jubarte is an in-process Rust Word-document engine for comparison, inspection, edit plans, tracked-change resolution, Markdown conversion, legacy DOC import, validation, scrubbing and PDF/PNG rendering. Native CLI, PyO3/Python and wasm-bindgen/Node/browser surfaces call the shared engine (src/lib.rs:7-35; jubarte-python/Cargo.toml:35-39; jubarte-wasm/Cargo.toml:18-32). A separately installed Python MCP server brokers document tools over stdio under one directory capability; the Gemini extension starts this server with workspacePath as its root (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108,373-381; gemini-extension.json:5-9). Native CLI self-update is a distinct optional network-and-executable-replacement workflow. Tag releases, local registry publication, CI and external Jules review/remediation are conditional maintainer workflows, not document-runtime capabilities.
Jubarte is a local Rust Word-document toolkit exposed through Rust byte APIs, PyO3 Python, WASM/Node, native and language CLIs, and an optional Python MCP server over stdio. Untrusted DOCX/DOC/Markdown and JSON edit plans feed package admission, XML/legacy parsers, comparisons, edits and PDF/PNG rendering. Native publication and explicit self-update are separate host-authority boundaries (src/lib.rs:7-30,106-174; src/convert/mod.rs:769-798; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-112,373-381). An independent architecture reviewer identified the resource rows below before its execution was interrupted; parent verified their actual consumers offline.

Its architecture summary: Jubarte is an in-process Word document engine exposing Rust byte APIs, a native CLI, PyO3/Python APIs and CLI, wasm-bindgen byte APIs and a Node CLI. Host-process memory/CPU availability. Inspection/edit defaults admit 64 MiB compressed, 64 MiB per part, 256 MiB inflated, 10,000 entries and XML depth 256; comparison and rendering use 512 MiB compressed/per part and 2 GiB inflated, with the same entry/depth caps (src/admission.rs:63-99; src/inspect.rs:604-620; src/document_comparer.rs:4926-4927; src/convert/mod.rs:769-778).

Filesystem authority granted to MCP: the existing expanded/resolved --root directory, default current directory, held through _OutputRoot. Edit artifacts are root/out_dir/{clean.docx,redline.docx,patch.diff,report.json}, optionally redline.pdf and redline-page-NN.png; rendering emits root/out_dir/page-NN.png and optional render.pdf (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:69-108,185-217,234-255,373-381; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1244-1278).

Ambient native/Python renderer fonts and persistent font index. JUBARTE_FONT_DIR overrides platform user-font locations; JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX overrides the index, with empty/off disabling it. Defaults resolve to ~/Library/Application Support/jubarte/font-index.tsv on macOS, $XDG_DATA_HOME/jubarte/font-index.tsv or ~/.local/share/jubarte/font-index.tsv on Unix, and %APPDATA%/jubarte/font-index.tsv on Windows. The index is beside, not inside, fonts, and saves via a sibling .tsv.<pid>.tmp file (src/convert/font.rs:2633-2652,3090-3107,3182-3229).

Native CLI operators select ambient input/output paths. src/bin/jubarte.rs:261-273 invokes publication::publish_paths, whose root=None backend opens output parents with ambient authority (src/publication.rs:203-225,431-446). Outputs stage beside their destination in .jubarte-<UUID>.partial/bytes, with Unix staging directory mode 0700 and exclusive creation (src/publication.rs:472-505). Python and Node CLI callers retain ambient local filesystem authority. Python's _read_side consumes caller paths and _write calls Path.write_bytes; Node's read and write helpers call fs.readFileSync/writeFileSync (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:73-83,126-133; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:52-56,106-111). The MCP operator grants a directory root once; a connected stdio client can invoke all registered read/write tools within that grant. --root defaults to current working directory, is expanded/resolved, and must be a directory; no HTTP listener or application authentication is configured in this entrypoint (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:373-381). Python containment checks are early diagnostics; actual reads and publications use _native._OutputRoot, backed by cap_std directory authority and portable relative-write validation (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:69-108; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1244-1278; src/publication.rs:153-199,228-273,431-463). overwrite is a per-call replacement capability, defaulting false. CLI Markdown image targets cross into local filesystem reads only through a selected resource root: explicit --resource-path wins, otherwise the Markdown file's parent, otherwise '.' (src/bin/jubarte.rs:2937-2943). The loader canonicalizes and holds that directory capability, applies image policy and reads relative to the capability; URLs are not fetched by this loader (src/bin/jubarte.rs:2851-2877). Native renderer font discovery is ambient OS-account access, independent of MCP's document/output root. JUBARTE_FONT_DIR overrides per-user locations; absent it, Windows uses APPDATA/jubarte/fonts, macOS HOME/Library/Application Support/jubarte/fonts, and other native platforms XDG_DATA_HOME/jubarte/fonts or HOME/.local/share/jubarte/fonts (src/convert/font.rs:2633-2652). Native discovery also examines named system/Word font directories and HOME/Library/Group Containers/UBF8T346G9.Office/FontCache/4/CloudFonts/<family>; the document-supplied family must be a single normal path component for that derived cloud directory (src/convert/font.rs:2225-2236,2281-2309).

Browser/Node WASM callers pass byte arrays and JSON options into the engine. The bindings disable default engine features, omit native publication on wasm32 and support comparison-budget overrides; the binding explicitly warns that its 2 GiB inflated default can exceed practical WASM heap capacity (jubarte-wasm/Cargo.toml:18-23; src/lib.rs:163-165; jubarte-wasm/src/lib.rs:63-97). Hosting applications own admission tuning, upload authorization, origin policy, worker isolation and persistence.

Explicit jubarte self-update crosses from GitHub release metadata/assets into executable replacement. The script calls a downstream app checkout, but that application's implementation is absent from this repository and is not included as inspected architecture (scripts/release.sh:141-175).

Edit requests cross from caller-authored plans to document mutations. Native CLI users grant ambient authority through selected input/output paths. publish_paths opens and retains each actual parent rather than enforcing a global document root; staging uses an exclusive UUID directory and file, with Unix staging directory mode 0700. Publication is atomic per file and records partial commits/durability uncertainty rather than promising set-wide rollback (src/publication.rs:5-7,83-143,203-225,420-505).

The MCP connected client can invoke registered read and write tools within the root chosen by the server operator. Startup defaults --root to cwd, resolves it once and serves stdio. Python containment checks are preliminary diagnostics; actual document reads and output publication pass through native _OutputRoot and cap-std directory-relative operations. No per-tool user identity or tenant separation is established; tool annotations are hints, while OutputRoot owns filesystem confinement (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:54-55,67-108,373-381; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1244-1276; src/publication.rs:146-199).

Native font discovery/cache is a separate authority from document-root publication. Font-family lookup can inspect system, Word, cloud and configured user-font directories; cloud family names must be one normal path component. The index may read cached face paths and write its configured file outside the MCP root. Its enforcing boundary is host environment/filesystem authority, not OutputRoot (src/convert/font.rs:2225-2236,2263-2315,2633-2652,2855-2862,3098-3107,3154-3172,3213-3229).

WASM byte APIs do not receive native publication::OutputRoot because that module is compiled only outside wasm32. Python and WASM bindings disable engine default features and request only cli grammar, so optional self-update is not part of those engine dependencies. Node's separately shipped CLI grants ambient filesystem access through node:fs around the WASM engine; its read/write helpers are distinct from native staged publication (src/lib.rs:147-149,163-165; jubarte-python/Cargo.toml:35-39; jubarte-wasm/Cargo.toml:18-23; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:16-21,52-79,106-111).

Self-update is an explicit native CLI capability. It selects fixed jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines repository, platform archive and inner binary path; requests checksum verification and regular-file verification; prompts unless --yes, and --check does not install. Current keys leave signature verification disabled. Dependency-owned download, archive extraction and executable-swap behavior is not established merely by this wrapper (src/bin/jubarte.rs:3892-3896,4062-4073; src/update.rs:25-48,186-257,274-285,299-321).

Release publication is privileged operator/CI work, separate from document processing. CI triggers on v* tags, checks tag/package version, grants build jobs contents:read and release job contents:write, optionally signs assets with step-scoped ZIPSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY, then publishes dist/* using step-scoped GH_TOKEN. Local release script has packaging dry runs and version confirmation unless YES, then separately publishes crates.io, two npm packages and PyPI with configured credentials (.github/workflows/release.yml:15-21,31-49,230-264,278-308,317-322,356-369; scripts/release.sh:729-747,874-888,904-919,929-958,1039-1069).

Untrusted DOCX/ZIP/XML, legacy DOC, embedded images/fonts and edit plans enter the engine. Permissive parse_xdocument requires a prior gate (src/admission.rs:15-28,63-99; src/xmllinq/parse.rs:21-36).

MCP stdio client invokes document tools under operator --root (default cwd). Python resolves paths for diagnostics; native _OutputRoot owns confined reads/publication through a held capability. Annotations are hints, not caller authorization (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:55,67-108,373-381; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1244-1277; src/publication.rs:146-199).

Native CLI grants ambient paths with staged per-file publication. Native Markdown images use --resource-path or Markdown parent directory; URL schemes/canonical escape targets are refused, followed by capability-relative read (src/bin/jubarte.rs:2835-2876,2936-2943).

Self-update enters executable replacement only on explicit command and confirmation/--yes. RELEASE_KEYS=[] and FIRST_SIGNED_RELEASE=None mean checksum-only today; optional Ed25519 support is inactive (src/update.rs:25-48,120-125,198-258,274-285; docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:59-82).

Native rendering, including MCP rendering, has separate ambient font discovery/cache I/O: JUBARTE_FONT_DIR overrides user font roots; JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX controls index persistence independently of document-root grants (src/convert/font.rs:2633-2652,3098-3107,3192-3229).

PR workflows run checked-out code on self-hosted runners sharing the private mbx cache http://mbx-cache:7543, namespace jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines. Outgoing privacy certification has independent controls: the leaks XML decoder must honor supported UTF-16, matching business XML attributes must not inherit namespace-blind numeric exemptions, metadata discovery must follow actual property targets, and Part::load must consistently decode selected property XML. A fix to one does not subsume the others (src/scrub.rs:188-199,357-385,467-475,484-490,522-552; src/opc/mod.rs:560-564).

Eager embedded-font loading copies and retains each unknown alias/style even when runs do not use it. Resource accounting must distinguish stored bytes from decoded buffers and alias multiplicity; Arc container values do not imply resolved-part sharing (src/convert/mod.rs:806-809; src/convert/font_table.rs:177-193,205-231).

Document producer -> Rust package/XML consumers: caller-controlled ZIP records, part names, compressed data and XML cross into trusted process memory. Admission checks central/local ZIP consistency, special-entry defects, case-folded duplicate names, encryption/compression policy, streamed inflated-byte budgets and XML checks. InputLimitOverrides rejects unknown configuration fields. Evidence: src/admission.rs:103-138, src/admission.rs:439-553, src/opc/archive.rs:34-51. The library forbids unsafe Rust in its own code: src/lib.rs:86.

Library caller -> raw XML parser: parse_xdocument is intentionally permissive and allocates a character vector without applying input policy; try_parse_xdocument_with_limits validates before constructing its DOM. Callers choosing the raw API own prior admission and process limits. Evidence: src/xmllinq/parse.rs:88-135. Default tag limits are 1,024 attributes, 1,024-byte qualified attribute names, 64 MiB attribute values and 128 MiB start tags: src/xmllinq/parse.rs:48-57.

Legacy DOC producer -> legacy parser: supported conversion follows the separate compound-file/WordDocument/FIB/table pipeline rather than DOCX ZIP admission. Stream structure and encryption checks belong to legacy_doc, and process resource limits remain a host obligation. Evidence: src/legacy_doc.rs:174-216, src/legacy_doc.rs:765-795.

Edit-plan producer -> document transaction: version-1 source SHA-256 is checked when supplied; version-2 source SHA-256 is mandatory and checked after plan validation. Version-1 editing refuses packages containing XML signatures or vbaProject.bin. These integrity checks bind source bytes, not authenticated identity or human approval. Evidence: src/edit.rs:2072-2104, src/edit/v2_apply.rs:75-100.

MCP client -> document filesystem: all connected clients receive the tools installed by build_server, with document reads/publication mediated by _native._OutputRoot and cap_std::fs::Dir. --root defaults to Path.cwd(); expanded/resolved root is opened once. Python resolution checks provide diagnostics, while actual reads and writes use the persistent capability. No per-user authentication or tenant partition is implemented by this stdio adapter. Evidence: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:54-108, jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:373-381, jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1244-1276, src/publication.rs:146-199.

MCP mutation -> output publication: output paths must pass portable-relative-name validation; target symlinks/directories are refused, and overwrite=false uses atomic hard-link installation. All bytes are staged and verified before any commit; atomicity is per file, and errors can report an already committed subset. Unix staging directories use mode 0700; Windows inherits platform access controls. Evidence: src/publication.rs:83-143, src/publication.rs:168-199, src/publication.rs:228-245, src/publication.rs:431-512, src/publication.rs:535-570.

Local CLI caller -> ambient filesystem: native publish_paths holds destination-parent handles and stages outputs, but deliberately grants ambient local-path authority. Python CLI _write uses Path.write_bytes; Node CLI write uses fs.writeFileSync. Their preflight existence checks are distinct from native publication enforcement and must be reviewed independently. Evidence: src/bin/jubarte.rs:261-273, src/publication.rs:203-225, jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:101-103, jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:126-133, jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:76-79, jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:106-111.

Markdown image names -> native CLI resource loader: the trusted root is explicit --resource-path or the Markdown file's parent, falling back to '.'. URL schemes are refused, percent escapes are decoded before policy checks, canonicalized targets must remain under the root, and actual reads use OutputRoot. The general Markdown library instead accepts a caller-provided image callback, absent by default. Evidence: src/bin/jubarte.rs:2811-2878, src/bin/jubarte.rs:2936-2943, src/markdown/mod.rs:196-198, src/markdown/mod.rs:216-226.

Document font requests -> ambient native font discovery/index: document family names select parsed host fonts, including system, Word and cloud-cache locations and configured user fonts. Cloud-family names must be one normal path component. The persistent index records source paths and timestamps, reloads matching files and saves through a process-specific temporary filename followed by rename. These operations do not use the MCP OutputRoot. Evidence: src/convert/font.rs:2225-2236, src/convert/font.rs:2263-2315, src/convert/font.rs:2633-2652, src/convert/font.rs:3154-3172, src/convert/font.rs:3182-3229.

Operator -> updater -> installed executable: explicit self-update resolves releases from jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines, selects one platform archive and inner jubarte binary, requires checksum verification and registers an extracted-regular-file verification hook. Noninteractive installation needs --yes; --check only resolves availability; explicitly requested versions can downgrade. Signature verification is implemented but inactive with the current empty key list. Extraction, HTTP behavior and executable replacement are delegated to self_update and were not independently inspected here. Evidence: src/update.rs:25-48, src/update.rs:88-124, src/update.rs:144-161, src/update.rs:186-258, src/update.rs:307-321.

Maintainer/CI -> release consumers: tag-driven GitHub builds have contents:read, while the release job alone has contents:write. Optional ZIPSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY reaches the signing step and temporary $RUNNER_TEMP/zipsign.XXXXXX/keyN files; checksums are generated after signing. A separate local release script can publish crates.io, two npm packages, PyPI and a GitHub fallback release using operator credentials. Its typed version confirmation can be bypassed with the explicit --yes option, and security-check.sh runs even with --skip-gates. Evidence: .github/workflows/release.yml:15-25, .github/workflows/release.yml:51-89, .github/workflows/release.yml:230-321, scripts/release.sh:374-380, scripts/release.sh:655-660, scripts/release.sh:875-899, scripts/release.sh:919-959, scripts/release.sh:976-1012, scripts/release.sh:1039-1069.

PR content -> privileged review/remediation automation: one pinned reviewer receives JULES_API_KEY and a GitHub token with contents:read, pull-requests:write and checks:write, gated to same-repository non-Dependabot PRs, without local checkout. A different pinned companion-remediation action receives JULES_API_KEY and starts only for trusted arthrod author/dispatcher conditions; its requested mode is AUTO_CREATE_PR with require_plan_approval:false. Companion workflow document gates and prompts do not establish what the external action or Jules service enforces. Evidence: .github/workflows/jules-review.yml:17-50, .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:46-54, .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:65-102, .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:259-324.

Untrusted DOCX -> admission -> OPC/XML: admission checks pre-index budgets, duplicate decoded/case-folded part names, ZIP structural defects, safe names, bounded inflation and XML policy; it does not extract entries to disk (src/admission.rs:439-490,522-575,736-760,788-803). The shared checked ZIP opener applies structural defects independently of higher-level admission (src/opc/archive.rs:34-51).

Raw XML library caller -> DOM: try_parse_xdocument_with_limits validates before constructing a DOM; infallible parse_xdocument deliberately skips policy and requires caller validation. Attribute defaults are 1,024 attributes, 1,024-byte names, 64 MiB values and 128 MiB complete start tags (src/xmllinq/parse.rs:48-57,90-135). Low-level APIs must not inherit guarantees of higher-level admitted entrypoints merely by association.

Caller edit plan -> source snapshot -> candidate: v1 source_sha256 is optional, verified when supplied; every operation resolves against the untouched source, and preview/application share preparation. The native CLI additionally rereads and hashes the named source before first publication and checks output aliases/collisions (src/edit.rs:5-24,97-106,2073-2094; src/bin/jubarte.rs:1642-1655,1764-1823). A hash is a freshness/integrity guard, not user authentication.

Native CLI caller -> ambient output paths: publication opens and holds each parent, stages complete bytes in parent/.jubarte-<UUID>.partial/bytes, and commits per file. Existing files require overwrite/force. Set publication is not atomic; partial commits are reported. Ambient publication replaces a destination symlink itself instead of following its referent (src/publication.rs:168-174,203-225,421-514; src/bin/jubarte.rs:1764-1823).

MCP stdio client -> document files: --root defaults to cwd, resolves once, and becomes native OutputRoot authority. Path canonicalization is an early diagnostic; actual reads/writes use root-relative cap-std operations. Output paths reject nonportable names and output symlinks, and overwrite defaults false. All tools share this root; read/write annotations are hints rather than separate caller authorization (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:54-55,67-108,373-381; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1244-1278; src/publication.rs:146-199,228-245,431-462).

Native Markdown -> local image loader: explicit --resource-path overrides the Markdown input's parent, defaulting to '.', and grants that directory's read capability. Percent-decoded URL schemes and resolved paths outside the canonical root are refused; reads use the opened root capability (src/bin/jubarte.rs:2811-2877,2936-2943). npm's adapter rejects resource_path (jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:724-727).

Native render -> font filesystem/cache: JUBARTE_FONT_DIR overrides user font locations; otherwise macOS uses HOME/Library/Application Support/jubarte/fonts, Linux uses XDG_DATA_HOME/jubarte/fonts or HOME/.local/share/jubarte/fonts, Windows uses APPDATA/jubarte/fonts. System/Word font directories and cached face paths are separate ambient reads. Font index precedence is JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX, with empty/off disabling persistence, otherwise parent(user_font_dir)/font-index.tsv. Saves use the index path with extension tsv.<pid>.tmp followed by rename. These operations are outside OutputRoot enforcement (src/convert/font.rs:2263-2275,2281-2315,2637-2652,2855-2862,3095-3107,3156-3165,3183-3189,3213-3229).

Browser host -> WASM executable: default initialization fetches jubarte_wasm_bg.wasm beside the JavaScript module; the caller may supply another module/URL. This is a code-loading capability, distinct from document relationships. Browser/WASM byte APIs do not expose native publication; Python/npm host wrappers separately perform filesystem I/O (jubarte-wasm/npm/web/jubarte_wasm.js:2575-2594; src/lib.rs:163-165; Cargo.toml:150-153).

Explicit self-update caller -> GitHub release -> installed executable: fixed repository jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines, platform archive and SHA256SUMS.txt; noninteractive installation requires --yes, while --check only looks up. Selected versions may downgrade. The binary inside the archive is jubarte-<version>-<target>/jubarte[.exe]; an extracted-binary lstat hook requires a regular file. Current RELEASE_KEYS is empty and FIRST_SIGNED_RELEASE is None, so signatures are not enforced. Unix uses tar.gz and Windows zip; extraction/replacement are dependency-owned (src/update.rs:25-48,91-108,120-125,144-159,198-257,307-320; Cargo.toml:137-148).

Maintainer publication -> public registries/release consumers: v* tag workflow builds binaries and wheels with read-only job permissions, then a distinct contents:write job publishes GitHub assets. An MCP client can invoke exposed document tools and choose relative paths, plans and overwrite within the operator-granted root. It does not thereby possess arbitrary host-path, network, release or registry authority. Fork PR eligibility, GitHub workflow approval settings and self-hosted runner registration determine additional reachability; no assumption of repository-secret or runner-administrator control is needed or granted by this model.

A release-asset adversary would need authority over published release artifacts, beyond normal document input. Current checksum-only update trust means archive and matching checksum share the release service's authority; documentation acknowledges this limitation. Signing keys, registry credentials and repository-write tokens are separate capabilities (docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:59-80; src/update.rs:44-48).

External Jules actions receive explicitly configured credentials and repository context, but their internal authorization, remote session permissions and enforcement cannot be established from this repository's workflow declarations alone.

The assigned validated findings additionally distinguish a less-trusted local writer of a plan/index staging parent from a document supplier. A symlink overwrite requires a separate writable shared parent, predictable/observable process PID and victim-writable referent; ordinary document control does not grant those prerequisites.

A document supplier can control document bytes, ZIP/XML structure, relationships, embedded media/fonts, Markdown content and document metadata that callers choose to process. This does not grant control of trusted environment variables, arbitrary operator-selected paths, release credentials or executable installation decisions.

A connected MCP client can choose tool arguments, source files and output destinations inside the operator-granted root and request overwrite=true. These are existing tool capabilities; new security impact would require exceeding the root grant, unintended disclosure to another actor, bypassing promised replacement restrictions or attacking the host process.

A library/WASM caller can choose API input bytes and exposed options, including input-limit overrides. A hosted service may expose a narrower subset, but no such service deployment or tenant model is established by this repository.

A PR contributor can control PR source/text subject to repository contribution permissions and workflow event gates. Same-repository authorship, trusted-user session gates, self-hosted runner admission and external agent authority must be evaluated separately; fork authors are not automatically authorized for secret-bearing Jules workflows.

findings.title: Rendering a small DOCX table can exhaust host memory
findings.summary: An untrusted DOCX author can set huge positive w:gridSpan, w:gridBefore or w:gridAfter counts in a small, shallow table. Rendering sums those counts into grid occupancy and directly sizes column, preference and merge vectors. Counts of 1000000000/1073741824 request about 4 GB/4 GiB for f32 columns; 4294967295 requests approximately 16 GiB before additional allocations, despite package admission.

severity.rationale: An untrusted document can deterministically drive huge allocations through a public parser boundary. This compromises availability of the rendering process; shared-service exposure is conditional and process memory limits constrain the blast radius.
severity.changeConditions: Enforce derived resource/output bounds before allocation; process-isolated callers limit blast radius.

confidence.rationale: Static source tracing establishes the unbounded usize parsing and direct vector allocation after admission, with no semantic span budget. No application code was executed.

rootCause.summary:
cell_span parses gridSpan as usize with only a minimum of one; row_grid_skip accepts arbitrary positive usize gridBefore/gridAfter and represents them as placeholder spans. table_block retains RawCell.colspan, sums row occupancy without checked bounds and uses it for vec!/resize; resolve_table_merges separately resizes its open vector to col+span. Neither per-span, aggregate-column nor derived-allocation budgets intervene.
The additional validated trace also identifies grid_skip_cell retaining the skipped count at src/convert/mod.rs:14379 and the column-preference allocation at :14263. A common repair must reject excessive effective columns before RawCell/grid-sized preference or merge work, including 32-bit WASM and checked cumulative arithmetic.
Table dimensions derived from attacker-controlled numeric XML are treated as allocation sizes without an upper grid width, checked cumulative accounting or fallible layout budget.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Table column occupancy is derived directly from document-provided span and skip counts without a semantic ceiling or checked aggregate budget before Vec allocation.

findings.remediation: Enforce practical per-span and total-column budgets for gridSpan, gridBefore and gridAfter before excessive RawCell, column, preference or merge allocation/work. Use checked occupancy sums and col+span arithmetic, apply the same budget to every derived table vector, and return a typed resource-limit refusal on excess.

counterEvidence: ZIP, inflated bytes and XML nesting are bounded before layout.
The security policy recommends process CPU/memory limits; these limit damage to a worker but do not reject the document.

with_layout performs package admission at lines 773-774. Its compressed, inflated-byte, entry, XML-depth, and attribute budgets do not constrain the numeric value or derived grid occupancy. This path requires no altChunk. gridBefore/gridAfter share the same broken table-allocation control.

previousFindings.summary: An untrusted DOCX author can set huge positive w:gridSpan, w:gridBefore or w:gridAfter counts in a small, shallow table. Rendering sums those counts into grid occupancy and directly sizes column, preference and merge vectors. Counts of 1000000000/1073741824 request about 4 GB/4 GiB for f32 columns; 4294967295 requests approximately 16 GiB before additional allocations, despite package admission.

severity.rationale: An untrusted document can deterministically drive huge allocations through a public parser boundary. This compromises availability of the rendering process; shared-service exposure is conditional and process memory limits constrain the blast radius.
severity.changeConditions: Enforce derived resource/output bounds before allocation; process-isolated callers limit blast radius.

confidence.rationale: Static source tracing establishes the unbounded usize parsing and direct vector allocation after admission, with no semantic span budget. No application code was executed.

rootCause.summary:
cell_span parses gridSpan as usize with only a minimum of one; row_grid_skip accepts arbitrary positive usize gridBefore/gridAfter and represents them as placeholder spans. table_block retains RawCell.colspan, sums row occupancy without checked bounds and uses it for vec!/resize; resolve_table_merges separately resizes its open vector to col+span. Neither per-span, aggregate-column nor derived-allocation budgets intervene.
The additional validated trace also identifies grid_skip_cell retaining the skipped count at src/convert/mod.rs:14379 and the column-preference allocation at :14263. A common repair must reject excessive effective columns before RawCell/grid-sized preference or merge work, including 32-bit WASM and checked cumulative arithmetic.
Table dimensions derived from attacker-controlled numeric XML are treated as allocation sizes without an upper grid width, checked cumulative accounting or fallible layout budget.

previousFindings.remediation: Enforce practical per-span and total-column budgets for gridSpan, gridBefore and gridAfter before excessive RawCell, column, preference or merge allocation/work. Use checked occupancy sums and col+span arithmetic, apply the same budget to every derived table vector, and return a typed resource-limit refusal on excess.

counterEvidence: ZIP, inflated bytes and XML nesting are bounded before layout.
The security policy recommends process CPU/memory limits; these limit damage to a worker but do not reject the document.

Both validated sources trace public with_layout admission through the span parsers to column-vector allocation and merge bookkeeping. A gridSpan of 1000000000 fits native and wasm32 usize and requests about 4 GB for f32 widths; the other source gives 1073741824, requiring 4 GiB before additional vectors. findings.title: Processing renamed auxiliary XML bypasses XML depth limits
findings.summary: A DOCX author can put deeply nested auxiliary XML under a non-.xml/.rels suffix. Admission drains those bytes without XML policy, while rendering, revision listing, revision acceptance/rejection and comparison follow internal relationships and recursively build a DOM. Confirmed rendering parts include theme, styles, numbering, comments/commentsExtended, notes and headers/footers; get_revisions and comparison also parse renamed footnotes/endnotes. A small admitted package can terminate the native host or trap WASM. The assigned source additionally confirms eager relationship-selected fontTable parsing before font inspection, including renamed fontTable.bin.

severity.rationale: Untrusted document bytes cross a public parser boundary and can terminate the rendering process. External shared-service exposure is conditional; no code execution or file access is established.
severity.changeConditions: Effective per-document worker isolation limits impact; enforcing active XML policy on every consumed XML part removes this path.

confidence.rationale: Parent independently verified the extension-based admission gate, relationship-selected consumer and unchecked recursive parser. Runtime stack threshold was not tested.

rootCause.summary:
Admission chooses XML depth/tag checks by .xml/.rels filename and applies extension-independent checking only to the main part. Relationship-selected auxiliary consumers do not require XML suffixes or an enforcing content-type check: main_rel_part selects theme/styles/numbering, part_xml_by_rel_kind selects comments/notes, and header/footer relationship resolution loads bytes as XML. Their unchecked parse_xdocument calls reach recursive parse_element without a construction-depth bound. PartFs and Strict normalization add byte bounds but do not close this auxiliary XML-policy gap.
The assigned source further records the converter's comment-thread path: part_xml_by_rel_kind loads comments/commentsExtended, then unchecked parsing occurs at src/convert/mod.rs:7669-7675 and :7688-7689. This shares the missing extension-independent XML admission control; the separately checked src/comments.rs:467-468 CommentFamily::load is excluded.
Revision listing and comparison independently share the same extension-based policy gap: document_comparer::notes_part_names resolves internal footnotes/endnotes targets regardless of filename, and get_revisions (:6318-6328) and compare notes parse_part_root (:6676-6689) call unchecked parse_xdocument on those actual strings. A central active-limit XML-consumption boundary covering all these consumers subsumes every source; fixing renderer-only calls would leave revision/comparison paths reachable.
Admission infers XML coverage from a filename suffix, but consumers infer XML from relationship role. The consumer trusts admission for parts the gate never parsed.
The discovery-0009 rendering trace additionally specifies a normal Transitional package and disabled link styles, leaving selected styles.bin nesting unchanged through load_stylesheet; neither filename/content-type enforcement nor later auxiliary admission intervenes. Markdown Package::xml separately checks its XML and is excluded from this trace.
The revision_processor trace resolves headers, footers, endnotes, footnotes, comments and styles without extension constraints, then parses selected XML both during RevisionIds collection (:3785-3794) and process_part transforms (:3732-3748). The suffix admission gap precedes these independent operation paths.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): Admission trusts filename extensions to identify XML, but the consumer identifies auxiliary XML by relationship type and invokes recursive unchecked parsing.

findings.remediation: Apply active InputLimits at a centralized checked XML access/parse boundary for every semantic XML consumer regardless of filename, or resolve/classify and admit XML through actual content-type/relationship use. Cover theme, styles, numbering, converter comments/commentsExtended, notes and headers/footers; include settings in regression coverage while retaining the source distinction that it was recommended rather than confirmed here. Preserve renamed-main checks, and enforce actual DOM construction depth or use iterative construction. Apply that same mandatory checked boundary to get_revisions and comparison notes parsing, including both footnotes and endnotes; propagate typed refusal under the active comparer InputLimits. Include pre_process_markup's relationship-selected notes at src/document_comparer.rs:4725-4750 and exposed Python get_revisions_json/WASM getRevisions; valid arbitrary part names remain supported. Include diagram and text-box relationship targets in regression coverage as proposed subcases, without promoting them to newly validated affected consumers. Cover revision_processor RevisionIds collection and process_part for all six selected auxiliary buckets (headers, footers, endnotes, footnotes, comments and styles), including public revision acceptance/rejection. Explicitly include the now-confirmed fontTable loader (src/convert/font_table.rs:66-78; src/convert/mod.rs:806) in the mandatory checked XML boundary; parsing must be bounded before any font root/entry inspection.

rootCause.summary: `admit()` chooses XML policy by `.xml`/`.rels` suffix and separately checks only the main document. Rendering locates auxiliary XML by relationship type, which permits arbitrary internal filenames, then uses `parse_xdocument()` without validation. Thus an attacker can store a deeply nested theme or stylesheet in a `.bin` part and reach `Parser::parse_element()` recursion despite the configured depth of 256. The same relationship-driven bypass reaches converter comments/commentsExtended, footnotes, endnotes and header/footer parsing; these share the missing admission discovery control.

extensions.semanticReductionNotes:

rootCause.summary:
Admission chooses XML depth/tag checks by .xml/.rels filename and applies extension-independent checking only to the main part. Relationship-selected auxiliary consumers do not require XML suffixes or an enforcing content-type check: main_rel_part selects theme/styles/numbering, part_xml_by_rel_kind selects comments/notes, and header/footer relationship resolution loads bytes as XML. Their unchecked parse_xdocument calls reach recursive parse_element without a construction-depth bound. PartFs and Strict normalization add byte bounds but do not close this auxiliary XML-policy gap.
The assigned source further records the converter's comment-thread path: part_xml_by_rel_kind loads comments/commentsExtended, then unchecked parsing occurs at src/convert/mod.rs:7669-7675 and :7688-7689. This shares the missing extension-independent XML admission control; the separately checked src/comments.rs:467-468 CommentFamily::load is excluded.
Revision listing and comparison independently share the same extension-based policy gap: document_comparer::notes_part_names resolves internal footnotes/endnotes targets regardless of filename, and get_revisions (:6318-6328) and compare notes parse_part_root (:6676-6689) call unchecked parse_xdocument on those actual strings. A central active-limit XML-consumption boundary covering all these consumers subsumes every source; fixing renderer-only calls would leave revision/comparison paths reachable.

previousFindings.remediation: Apply active InputLimits at a centralized checked XML access/parse boundary for every semantic XML consumer regardless of filename, or resolve/classify and admit XML through actual content-type/relationship use. rootCause.summary:
Admission chooses XML depth/tag checks by .xml/.rels filename and applies extension-independent checking only to the main part. Relationship-selected auxiliary consumers do not require XML suffixes or an enforcing content-type check: main_rel_part selects theme/styles/numbering, part_xml_by_rel_kind selects comments/notes, and header/footer relationship resolution loads bytes as XML. Their unchecked parse_xdocument calls reach recursive parse_element without a construction-depth bound. PartFs and Strict normalization add byte bounds but do not close this auxiliary XML-policy gap.
The assigned source further records the converter's comment-thread path: part_xml_by_rel_kind loads comments/commentsExtended, then unchecked parsing occurs at src/convert/mod.rs:7669-7675 and :7688-7689. This shares the missing extension-independent XML admission control; the separately checked src/comments.rs:467-468 CommentFamily::load is excluded.
Revision listing and comparison independently share the same extension-based policy gap: document_comparer::notes_part_names resolves internal footnotes/endnotes targets regardless of filename, and get_revisions (:6318-6328) and compare notes parse_part_root (:6676-6689) call unchecked parse_xdocument on those actual strings. A central active-limit XML-consumption boundary covering all these consumers subsumes every source; fixing renderer-only calls would leave revision/comparison paths reachable.
Admission infers XML coverage from a filename suffix, but consumers infer XML from relationship role. The consumer trusts admission for parts the gate never parsed.

previousFindings.remediation: Apply active InputLimits at a centralized checked XML access/parse boundary for every semantic XML consumer regardless of filename, or resolve/classify and admit XML through actual content-type/relationship use. Cover theme, styles, numbering, converter comments/commentsExtended, notes and headers/footers; include settings in regression coverage while retaining the source distinction that it was recommended rather than confirmed here. Preserve renamed-main checks, and enforce actual DOM construction depth or use iterative construction. Apply that same mandatory checked boundary to get_revisions and comparison notes parsing, including both footnotes and endnotes; propagate typed refusal under the active comparer InputLimits. Include pre_process_markup's relationship-selected notes at src/document_comparer.rs:4725-4750 and exposed Python get_revisions_json/WASM getRevisions; valid arbitrary part names remain supported.

validation.summary:
The validated styles-specific trace confirms a normal main document can select deeply nested styles.bin, without suffix/content-type enforcement or a later depth gate. The other validated trace confirms theme1.bin plus styles, numbering, comments, footnotes, endnotes and relationship-named headers/footers. Byte, inflation, CRC, ZIP/path checks and the nonstandard-main exception remain active; the malicious auxiliary payload alone bypasses XML policy. No external relationship or network fetch is needed.
The additional validated trace confirms converter commentsExtended as well as comments/notes/chrome consumers. A roughly 700 KiB part with 100000 nested elements fits byte limits; actual failing depth remains runtime-dependent and unmeasured. For a normal Transitional DOCX, normalization leaves the renamed part unchanged (src/strict_translation.rs:809-831); PartFs adds byte bounds rather than XML policy. This does not affect separately validated CommentFamily::load (src/comments.rs:467-468).
Verified public `get_revisions` input admission, internal relationship resolution without suffix restrictions, bounded ZIP loading that does not validate auxiliary XML, and the recursive parser sink. The comparison notes pipeline has the same missing check.
Parent verified suffix gate, main-only fallback, relationship resolver and get_revisions parser plus Python/WASM exposure. Deep notes.dat XML is parsed before note-definition processing. pre_process_markup independently follows and parses the same relationship-selected parts at4725-4750.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Attacker DOCX styles relationship -> main_rel_part -> part_string(styles.bin) -> load_stylesheet -> Dom::parse_xdocument -> recursive parse_element.

rootCause.summary:
Admission chooses XML depth/tag checks by .xml/.rels filename and applies extension-independent checking only to the main part. Relationship-selected auxiliary consumers do not require XML suffixes or an enforcing content-type check: main_rel_part selects theme/styles/numbering, part_xml_by_rel_kind selects comments/notes, and header/footer relationship resolution loads bytes as XML. Their unchecked parse_xdocument calls reach recursive parse_element without a construction-depth bound. PartFs and Strict normalization add byte bounds but do not close this auxiliary XML-policy gap.
The assigned source further records the converter's comment-thread path: part_xml_by_rel_kind loads comments/commentsExtended, then unchecked parsing occurs at src/convert/mod.rs:7669-7675 and :7688-7689. This shares the missing extension-independent XML admission control; the separately checked src/comments.rs:467-468 CommentFamily::load is excluded.
Revision listing and comparison independently share the same extension-based policy gap: document_comparer::notes_part_names resolves internal footnotes/endnotes targets regardless of filename, and get_revisions (:6318-6328) and compare notes parse_part_root (:6676-6689) call unchecked parse_xdocument on those actual strings. A central active-limit XML-consumption boundary covering all these consumers subsumes every source; fixing renderer-only calls would leave revision/comparison paths reachable.
Admission infers XML coverage from a filename suffix, but consumers infer XML from relationship role. The consumer trusts admission for parts the gate never parsed.
The discovery-0009 rendering trace additionally specifies a normal Transitional package and disabled link styles, leaving selected styles.bin nesting unchanged through load_stylesheet; neither filename/content-type enforcement nor later auxiliary admission intervenes. Markdown Package::xml separately checks its XML and is excluded from this trace.

findings.title: Shallow malformed XML can bypass admission and overflow the DOM parser stack
findings.summary:
A DOCX main part containing many sibling `

` tags passes the tolerant admission depth check as shallow empty elements. The DOM parser consumes the two slashes as attribute quotes and treats those siblings as nested open elements, enabling stack exhaustion despite the configured XML depth limit.

severity.rationale: A small attacker-authored document can cause unbounded parser recursion in the host process through a public parser boundary. Impact is availability loss; shared service use and process isolation determine wider impact.

confidence.rationale: Independent source review confirmed both product parser paths and cached quick-xml 0.42.0 tokenization: final /> is stripped into an Empty event and HTML attributes accept the remaining unquoted slash.

taxonomy.category: Uncontrolled recursion caused by parser disagreement

rootCause.summary:
The admission gate allows HTML-style unquoted attributes, while the downstream parser assumes any first character after `=` opens a quoted value. For `

` admission sees an empty tag with an unquoted slash value. DOM parsing consumes both slashes as delimiters, sees an ordinary closing `>` and recursively nests following siblings. Thus reader depth is not the depth of the representation actually constructed.

findings.remediation: Make tolerant attribute tokenization identical between admission and DOM construction or refuse unsupported unquoted values, and enforce a real construction-depth limit or use an iterative DOM parser.

counterEvidence: Admission checks matching end tags, XML depth and tag budgets; these checks apply to quick-xml's different interpretation.
The strict checked XML API rejects unquoted attributes, but package admission deliberately uses the tolerant mode.
limitations: No adversarial application input was executed.
Exact stack-overflow threshold is host/build dependent.

Repeat sibling

elements under w:body. quick-xml parses these as Empty with tag p a=/; TagPolicy::tolerant uses html_attributes and permits unquoted value /. Admission sees depth 2. Permissive Parser::parse_element lines 574-593 blindly treats first / after = as opening quote, consumes second / as closing quote, leaving > and treating the empty element as an OPEN element; at line 661 recursively parses each following sibling as child => unbounded recursion despite max_xml_depth256.

findings.title: Reading or converting nested legacy DOC fields can monopolize the processing thread

rootCause.summary:
The public legacy reader decodes WordDocument and 0Table/1Table pieces into StoryChar, preserving field delimiters, then calls Story::blocks with no field-work/depth budget. blocks retains enclosing code/result states in Vec<bool> and recomputes fields.iter().any for each character, including begin/separator/end controls. Repeated begin+separator sets prior frames false, defeating short-circuiting; balanced ends scan shrinking false stacks and displayed results scan all enclosing frames. No O(1) active-code count is maintained.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Story::blocks recomputes whether any field is in its code phase by scanning all nested field flags on each character, with no nesting/work limit or constant-time aggregate state.

findings.remediation: Maintain an O(1) active-code-frame count, updating it correctly on begin, separator and end while preserving suppression under any code ancestor. Enforce explicit field-nesting and processing-work budgets for balanced and malformed legacy field streams before excessive work.

validation.summary:
Both validated source traces establish public legacy read/CLI conversion -> main_text -> Story::blocks without a field-depth budget. N begin/separator pairs incur O(N²) Boolean visits; balanced closing controls and result text add scans. At depth 100000, roughly 300 KiB of balanced delimiters requires billions of Boolean examinations. The additional native read_document refusal path invokes legacy_doc::read to decide whether to print a DOC conversion hint, so refusal is not an early protection.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Unencrypted DOC -> legacy_doc::read -> main_text -> Story::blocks -> fields.iter().any on each character; BEGIN pushes true, SEPARATOR changes top to false, END pops.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent read main_text control decoding and Story::blocks. Each0x13 pushes true;0x14 makes the newest entry false. Repeating this pair leaves all ancestors false and causes scans summing1+2+...+N; balanced0x15 closes also scan before popping. Physical CFB bounds do not constrain this later work.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): For [0x13,0x14] repeated N times followed by N 0x15 markers, the stack grows then shrinks while mostly/all false. Sum of traversed depths is quadratic; N=100000 uses 300000 physical text bytes and tens of billions of predicate checks.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Verified public read decodes piece-table text to StoryChar values and calls Story::blocks; compressed and UTF-16 decoders preserve field control characters. Each start/separator pair grows an all-false stack, so iter().any scans a progressively larger prefix. No field-depth cap intervenes in the inspected path.

rootCause.summary:
with_layout expands document-selected altChunk bytes after original ZIP/XML admission. HTML Builder::start accepts a colspan up to usize::MAX, end_table sums spans and emits gridCol once per declared column. No maximum column count or generated-WML byte budget is passed into expand, so a short HTML table can demand gigabytes before parser/output safeguards can act. The assigned corroborating trace follows Builder::start, end_cell, HTML tokenizer close/end_table dispatch, per-row span summation and the pre-DOM grid-generation loop; page/raster limits occur later.
The HTML importer treats document-supplied colspan as a trusted expansion count. It sums spans and serializes a physical XML column for every claimed slot without checking a maximum or generated byte budget.

findings.remediation: Enforce a practical maximum cell span and checked per-row/aggregate column counts before generating any table XML. Charge all HTML/MHT-generated WML, including repeated/nested tables, to a cumulative byte/work budget inside altChunk expansion and return a typed input-limit refusal before allocation or DOM construction.

findings.title: Flat LaTeX script chains bypass nesting limits and exhaust the writer stack
findings.summary: Converting untrusted Markdown with a long flat superscript/subscript chain builds an attacker-deep AST despite the parser's nesting limit. The recursive OMML writer then exhausts the native stack or traps a WASM instance.

severity.rationale: Default processing of an untrusted document can exhaust worker CPU/stack; impact is availability, with blast radius dependent on process isolation.
severity.changeConditions: Enforcing the missing input/derived-work boundary removes this path; isolated workers reduce shared-service impact.

confidence.rationale: Independent worker and parent verified the concrete input-to-sink control failure statically; exact runtime resource/failure thresholds were not measured.

codeEvidence.explanation: The XML emitter passes the caller's LaTeX to math::omml.

codeEvidence.label: Parser-call depth is bounded
codeEvidence.explanation: The limit ends when each argument returns; it does not describe existing node depth.

codeEvidence.label: Flat tokens repeatedly wrap previous output
codeEvidence.explanation: Each new script takes the prior already nested node as its base.

codeEvidence.label: A script can consume just one character
codeEvidence.explanation: Repeated ^1 segments do not keep parser depth elevated.

codeEvidence.label: Scripts retain the whole prior base
codeEvidence.explanation: Each wrapping operation creates another structural AST level.

codeEvidence.label: Existing Scripts nodes are retained intact
codeEvidence.explanation: Non-text nodes become the next base without depth validation.

codeEvidence.label: Writer recursively traverses nodes
codeEvidence.explanation: argument calls nodes, and nodes invokes node again.

codeEvidence.label: Script base recurses without a budget
codeEvidence.explanation: The writer descends the attacker-deep base.

codeEvidence.label: OMML serializes the parsed AST directly
codeEvidence.explanation: No AST-depth gate separates parse result from recursive writer.

rootCause.summary: The nesting guard tracks recursive parser calls. nested_list instead iteratively takes its previous output node as a new script base, preserving existing Scripts nodes through take_base. Each one-character script argument finishes before the next wrapper is added, so parse depth remains shallow while AST depth grows with input length. Writer::node recurses into that unbounded base through argument/nodes; no AST-depth or iterative traversal/destruction control intervenes.

findings.remediation: Bound actual AST depth and work when wrapping previous script/prime bases, and use iterative writing and safe nonrecursive destruction so rejection cannot itself drop an attacker-deep tree recursively.

counterEvidence: The 64-level parser guard protects recursively nested groups/commands, not this iterative AST wrapping.
No runtime threshold or crafted input was measured; exact stack/trap behavior is platform-dependent.
limitations: No application code, tests, exploit input or network activity executed.
validation.summary: Parent verified the 64 parser-call limit, one-character argument consumption, iterative wrapping, preservation of prior Scripts nodes, nonrecursive merge behavior, and unguarded writer recursion. A flat a^1^1... expression can therefore create arbitrary AST depth without violating the guarded syntax depth. markdown_to_docx assembles math by calling math::omml, which directly serializes equation(latex).

dataflow.summary: Markdown math -> markdown_to_docx -> package/XML emitter -> math::omml -> Parser::nested_list/take_base/scripts -> deeply nested Node::Scripts -> Writer::node/argument/nodes -> stack exhaustion

returnedFinding.title: Flat LaTeX script chains bypass the nesting guard and overflow the writer stack
returnedFinding.attacker: A party supplying Markdown converted through the public Markdown-to-DOCX API or corresponding CLI/binding.
returnedFinding.violated_security_invariant: The math nesting limit must bound the depth of the AST subsequently traversed and destroyed, including depth created by iterative wrapping.
returnedFinding.source_to_sink: For each superscript or subscript, nested_list removes the previous output node and wraps it in a new Node::Scripts. A flat expression such as a^1^1^1 repeatedly wraps the existing AST while parser call depth stays shallow. The OMML writer recursively visits each script's base through node -> argument -> nodes -> node, with no AST-depth check.
returnedFinding.concrete_impact: Markdown consisting of '$a' followed by roughly 100000 repetitions of '^1' and a closing '$' creates an approximately 100000-level AST from about 200 KB of input. Writing or dropping that tree can exhaust the native stack or trap the WASM instance.

omml directly invokes writer.nodes(&equation(latex)) at math.rs:1943.

findings.title: WMF record-boundary failures amplify polygon work and retained text
findings.summary: Rendering a DOCX with a crafted placeable WMF lets short declared records consume payload from later records, which the outer parser then revisits. Polygon/polypolygon/polyline records can cause billions of coordinate decodes from roughly 512 KiB; EXTTEXTOUT/TEXTOUT records can retain hundreds of megabytes of overlapping owned strings from roughly 205.6 KB. The common missing record-local boundary bypasses the canvas cap and original package budgets. A further framing uses alternating six-byte EXTTEXTOUT and unknown 0xFFFF record headers to claim 65,535 text bytes from subsequent records, implying several GiB of retained strings from roughly 1 MiB of media; this is a static estimate.

severity.rationale: Default document rendering can amplify a small embedded WMF into excessive coordinate/raster work or large retained text allocations, affecting host-process or WASM availability. Shared-host blast radius depends on caller process isolation; no memory-unsafe out-of-bounds read, disclosure or code execution is established.
severity.changeConditions: Mandatory record-local parsing and validated counts across all WMF handlers remove the overlapping-payload amplification; cumulative work/text budgets and isolated workers constrain resource effects.

confidence.rationale: Independent worker and parent verified the concrete input-to-sink control failure statically; exact runtime resource/failure thresholds were not measured.

rootCause.summary:
raster_wmf checks declared size*2 against remaining file bytes but keeps passing the entire data slice to its handlers, then advances only by the declared record size. Polygon, polypolygon and polyline counts therefore cause coordinate reads/allocation/raster work across later records. Independently, META_EXTTEXTOUT/META_TEXTOUT counts slice later bytes as text; wmf_text decodes owned Strings retained in texts and ultimately ImageKind::Metafile. Both subcases repeatedly consume overlapping suffixes because consumed payload extent is not tied to outer advancement. EMF's analogous point helper checks off+size. A mandatory record-limited slice plus record-local field/count checks at this shared WMF dispatch boundary fixes all absorbed handlers; geometry-only count patches leave text retention reachable.
With size=3 the outer cursor advances six bytes. EXTTEXTOUT's count at payload+4 can come from the next unknown-0xFFFF header; options may select a later optional-rectangle string offset. Subsequent header bytes repeatedly supply large whole-file text spans. Both drawing and VML image relationships reach this decoder before the general image crate's default 512 MiB allocation limit, which therefore cannot bound this earlier retention. The supplied alternating-header proof gives options=3, selecting the optional-rectangle branch and a string start at payload+16.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): WMF variable-length record data is read against the whole input rather than the record's declared slice; declared record progression permits overlapping unbounded amplification.

findings.remediation: Confine every WMF handler, including field, font, string and geometry reads, to a slice limited to its checked declared record extent. Before allocation validate fixed fields, ring/point counts and coordinate arrays, EXTTEXTOUT options/optional rectangle and text count, and TEXTOUT padded string plus trailing coordinates against that slice using checked arithmetic. Refuse inconsistent records before decoding/rasterization/replay and enforce cumulative decoded-text, record and total geometry/work budgets. Keep the already bounded EMF behavior.

validation.summary:
Parent independently read raster_wmf dispatch/record checks and all three polygon handlers, their file-wide reads and outer offset increment. Repeated eight-byte polygon records with point-count 65535 can repeatedly consume later record bytes as coordinate payload; a 512KiB file supports more than two billion decodes before a late truncation refusal. This is bounded by whole-file bytes rather than record bytes; no memory out-of-bounds access is claimed.
Verified that text counts are u16, checked against the entire buffer, and do not need to fit the declared record. A 14-byte EXTTEXTOUT record can claim 65,535 text bytes beyond its own end. Ten thousand such records with enough trailing bytes imply 655,350,000 source bytes decoded into retained Strings from about 205.6 KB of WMF; UTF-8 conversion and later text handling can add cost.
Additional static proof: a placeable WMF with nonzero mapping bounds and fourteen-byte EXTTEXTOUT records (y/x/count/options, options zero, n=65535, no record-local text) reads following records into retained strings. Tens of thousands of such records in roughly 1 MB imply several GB of overlapping decoded text. This is an estimate from the supplied source, not executed memory measurement; ordinary bounds, nonblank content and sufficient trailing data are prerequisites.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent confirmed size3 advances6 bytes, EXTTEXTOUT reads count at payload+4, string at payload+8/16 and checks only data.get(at..at+n). Alternating six-byte EXTTEXTOUT/unknown0xFFFF headers supply count65535 from the next header while allowing repeated advancement. ansi_text collects owned strings retained in texts. TEXTOUT shares the record-local bounds omission.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Verified the record cursor at metafile.rs:684 advances by size2 while handlers at 603-620 read against data. Approximately 65536 14-byte records plus 65535 trailing bytes fit in ~1 MiB yet retain at least ~4 GiB of text. WMF detection checks the placeable magic; bounded canvas dimensions do not bound text. Package admission permits such small binary media.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent inspected WMF dispatch, header/canvas setup, complete record loop (445-687), ansi_text (430-442) and wmf_text retention (692-716). Repeated eight-byte TEXTOUT records (4 words) can each declare 65535 bytes, with coordinates and tail inside the overall file and an EOF before unused tail; nonzero extents and nonblank bytes satisfy retention. EXTTEXTOUT and all three point-array opcodes share the boundary failure.
Additional assigned static framing: roughly 100000 eight-byte TEXTOUT records each claiming 65535 bytes plus sufficient trailing bytes (EOF before unused tail) fit in roughly 1 MiB and imply several GiB of overlapping retained strings. Nonzero mapping extents and nonblank decoded text are required. Matching short POLYGON/POLYLINE counts imply billions of point iterations. No payload or measurement was executed.

rootCause.summary: `decode_image()` routes embedded WMF bytes into `raster_wmf()`. The parser validates only that `size2` fits the remaining file; handlers still receive the entire `data` buffer. `EXTTEXTOUT` and `TEXTOUT` use attacker counts in whole-file slices without requiring those slices to fit the current record. `wmf_text()` allocates a String for each such slice, and `texts` retains it while the cursor advances by only the small declared record size. finding.remediation: Slice every WMF record to its declared extent and make all field, string, font and point reads relative to that slice. Reject inconsistent lengths before copying/replay and enforce aggregate text/geometry work budgets.

extensions.semanticReductionNotes: The supplied static proof framing uses repeated eight-byte WMF polygon records with count 65535. previousFindings.title: WMF record-boundary failures amplify polygon work and retained text
previousFindings.summary: Rendering a DOCX with a crafted placeable WMF lets short declared records consume payload from later records, which the outer parser then revisits. Polygon/polypolygon/polyline records can cause billions of coordinate decodes from roughly 512 KiB; EXTTEXTOUT/TEXTOUT records can retain hundreds of megabytes of overlapping owned strings from roughly 205.6 KB. The common missing record-local boundary bypasses the canvas cap and original package budgets.

severity.rationale: Default document rendering can amplify a small embedded WMF into excessive coordinate/raster work or large retained text allocations, affecting host-process or WASM availability. Shared-host blast radius depends on caller process isolation; no memory-unsafe out-of-bounds read, disclosure or code execution is established.
severity.changeConditions: Mandatory record-local parsing and validated counts across all WMF handlers remove the overlapping-payload amplification; cumulative work/text budgets and isolated workers constrain resource effects.

confidence.rationale: Independent worker and parent verified the concrete input-to-sink control failure statically; exact runtime resource/failure thresholds were not measured.

rootCause.summary: raster_wmf checks declared size*2 against remaining file bytes but keeps passing the entire data slice to its handlers, then advances only by the declared record size. Polygon, polypolygon and polyline counts therefore cause coordinate reads/allocation/raster work across later records. Independently, META_EXTTEXTOUT/META_TEXTOUT counts slice later bytes as text; wmf_text decodes owned Strings retained in texts and ultimately ImageKind::Metafile. Both subcases repeatedly consume overlapping suffixes because consumed payload extent is not tied to outer advancement. EMF's analogous point helper checks off+size. A mandatory record-limited slice plus record-local field/count checks at this shared WMF dispatch boundary fixes all absorbed handlers; geometry-only count patches leave text retention reachable.

previousFindings.remediation: Confine every WMF handler to a slice limited to its checked declared record extent. Before allocation, validate fixed fields, ring/point counts and coordinate arrays, EXTTEXTOUT options/optional rectangle and text count, and TEXTOUT padded string plus trailing coordinates against that slice using checked arithmetic. Refuse malformed records before decoding/rasterization and enforce cumulative decoded-text, record and total-work budgets. Keep the already bounded EMF behavior.

counterEvidence: MAX_SIDE=384 bounds raster dimensions; it does not restrict how often subsequent bytes are parsed.
Safe slice reads eventually reject truncation, after earlier records have already performed amplified work.
EMF read_emf_points has record-end bounds; it does not protect the WMF handlers.
Whole-buffer slice checks prevent Rust memory unsafety; this is parser resource amplification.
WMF object count is clamped and canvas MAX_SIDE is 384, but neither controls the texts vector.
Valid record-local counts would consume input proportionally and would not produce this overlap.
limitations: No application code, tests, exploit input or network activity executed.
No runtime reproduction; exact heap growth/failure depends on String allocation and host limits.
Geometry siblings also use full-file readers; only the text-allocation consequences are independently validated here.

validation.summary:
Parent independently read raster_wmf dispatch/record checks and all three polygon handlers, their file-wide reads and outer offset increment. Repeated eight-byte polygon records with point-count 65535 can repeatedly consume later record bytes as coordinate payload; a 512KiB file supports more than two billion decodes before a late truncation refusal. Ten thousand such records with enough trailing bytes imply 655,350,000 source bytes decoded into retained Strings from about 205.6 KB of WMF; UTF-8 conversion and later text handling can add cost.

extensions.semanticReductionNotes:

META_POLYGON, META_POLYPOLYGON and META_POLYLINE all need record-local bounds; the 384-pixel canvas cap, whole-file safe reads and bounded EMF helper do not enforce those WMF record bounds.
dedup-0003 merges the same shared WMF record-slice violation, rather than a mere media/sink family match. Preserve both proof tuples and all five handlers: eight-byte polygon records with count 65535 in ~512 KiB yield >2 billion point decodes; 10000 fourteen-byte EXTTEXTOUT records claiming 65535 bytes with sufficient nonblank following data yield 655350000 source bytes decoded into retained Strings from ~205.6 KB. The text source independently validates its text consequences, while previous validated evidence establishes geometry consequences. Actual failure thresholds remain unmeasured. The common remediation limits the slice at dispatch for every handler; fixing only polygon handlers would not subsume the text source. MAX_SIDE=384, object-count clamps and safe whole-file reads remain useful but do not limit these repeated payloads.

rootCause.summary:

Polygon, polypolygon and polyline counts therefore cause coordinate reads/allocation/raster work across later records. Both subcases repeatedly consume overlapping suffixes because consumed payload extent is not tied to outer advancement. EMF's analogous point helper checks off+size. A mandatory record-limited slice plus record-local field/count checks at this shared WMF dispatch boundary fixes all absorbed handlers; geometry-only count patches leave text retention reachable.
With size=3 the outer cursor advances six bytes. EXTTEXTOUT's count at payload+4 can come from the next unknown-0xFFFF header; options may select a later optional-rectangle string offset. Subsequent header bytes repeatedly supply large whole-file text spans. Both drawing and VML image relationships reach this decoder before the general image crate's default 512 MiB allocation limit, which therefore cannot bound this earlier retention. The supplied alternating-header proof gives options=3, selecting the optional-rectangle branch and a string start at payload+16.

findings.title: Aliased legacy DOC pieces expand small physical text into enormous logical stories
findings.summary: Thousands of contiguous logical pieces can all reference the same physical text range. For example, 4095 pieces referencing one common 1 MiB compressed-text range describe nearly 4 GiB of logical characters while requiring only roughly 49 KiB of piece records. main_text materializes metadata for every character, requiring tens of GiB before rendering. A second source-derived framing uses approximately 65,535 pieces reusing 64 KiB, producing over four billion logical characters from a piece table below 1 MiB; expansion precedes later auxiliary-table checks.

severity.rationale: An untrusted document supplier can directly induce disproportionate resource use or bypass a resource admission control during normal parsing. Impact is availability of the processing worker/embedding process; no public deployment is assumed.
severity.changeConditions: Enforcing logical-work/selected-directory bounds removes the path; process isolation limits shared-service consequences.

confidence.rationale: Independent investigator and parent traced actual local source and effective controls. Resource counts are statically derived; no runtime reproduction or deployment is asserted.

rootCause.summary:
FIB ccp_text and per-piece CP endpoints are caller-controlled u32 values. pieces assigns each piece an independent physical offset, so many consecutive logical ranges can alias one physical text range. main_text verifies logical continuity and physical read bounds but then pushes one StoryChar per logical CP without a logical/output budget. Physical OLE bounds therefore do not limit retained logical metadata.
The decoder validates logical coverage and physical bounds independently but never limits cumulative decoded characters or charges repeated physical aliases for their full logical expansion. Contiguous increasing CPs may share FC backing; the rejected decreasing/repeated-logical-range variant is unnecessary. Piece count and total decoded work also need explicit accounting.

findings.remediation: Introduce configurable legacy physical-input, piece-count, cumulative logical-character, retained-metadata and expansion-work budgets. Check FIB ccp_text and checked cumulative piece lengths before materialization, charge every decoded character including repeated physical aliases, and return typed refusals through read/doc_to_markdown/doc_to_docx and CLI callers. Preserve legitimate fast-save aliases and split UTF-16 surrogate handling within budget.

counterEvidence: Checked arithmetic and word.get/u16_at refuse physical offsets outside WordDocument. Increasing CP validation prevents backwards logical pieces. Neither control bounds repeated physical-range references or total logical expansion. Public legacy APIs have no InputLimits parameter, and CLI parsing happens before resulting DOCX admission.
Compound-file parsing and character addressing use bounds/overflow checks.
main_text rejects decreasing logical CPs, gaps and physical out-of-bounds reads; the repeated in-range aliases satisfy these checks.
No malformed auxiliary table is needed because expansion runs first.
Sector chains are bounded and repeated FAT locations rejected; integer arithmetic and physical byte reads are checked.
Decreasing CPs and gaps are refused, so the rejected repeated 0..N logical-range proposal is not needed. This construction uses increasing contiguous CPs.
The repository recommends host process limits, which constrain damage but do not provide a bounded parser refusal.
Compound-file sector walks and numeric offsets use checked/bounded arithmetic; these bound physical reads, not logical reuse.
Main-story CP coverage must be continuous and increasing; the described pieces satisfy that condition.
Process memory/CPU limits are recommended by SECURITY.md and can contain the host impact.

confidence.rationale: Independently traced public read/doc_to_docx and CLI entrypoints through independent CP/FC fields to per-character retained allocation. Physical bounds and monotonicity checks do not prevent reuse. No runtime reproduction.

codeEvidence.label: Public legacy reader forwards untrusted piece metadata
codeEvidence.explanation: The attacker supplies both the FIB logical character count and piece-table entries. The public reader reaches text expansion before later style/table parsing.

codeEvidence.label: Logical character ranges and physical file offsets are independent
codeEvidence.explanation: Monotonic logical CP ranges can all carry the same valid physical FC; bytes need not be duplicated on disk.

codeEvidence.label: Every logical character creates retained output
codeEvidence.explanation: Iteration is controlled by the declared logical span, and the physical cursor resets for every piece. No cumulative logical character or output allocation budget is checked.

codeEvidence.label: StoryChar allocations accumulate across all pieces
codeEvidence.explanation: Each logical CP is retained with character, offsets and modifiers; repeated physical ranges therefore multiply allocation.

codeEvidence.label: CLI imports legacy DOC before package admission
codeEvidence.explanation: A normal convert operation automatically invokes the vulnerable reader for OLE input. Later DOCX admission cannot bound this earlier expansion.

rootCause.summary: The FIB and piece table independently provide total logical characters, logical CP ranges, and physical FC offsets. main_text checks monotonic coverage and each physical read, then expands every logical CP into an owned StoryChar. Reusing a valid physical text range across many logical pieces passes those checks while multiplying retained memory; no logical expansion budget precedes the loop.

finding.remediation: Enforce an explicit maximum logical story length and cumulative expanded bytes/work before iterating or allocating. Carry host InputLimits or equivalent legacy limits through all public DOC readers and CLI conversion; allow legitimate physical piece reuse only within that budget.

counterEvidence: Compound-file sector walks and numeric offsets use checked/bounded arithmetic; these bound physical reads, not logical reuse.
Main-story CP coverage must be continuous and increasing; the described pieces satisfy that condition.
Process memory/CPU limits are recommended by SECURITY.md and can contain the host impact.
limitations: No generated DOC or application execution; exact peak allocation and abort behavior were not measured.
validation.summary: Verified that 4095 consecutive compressed pieces of 1 MiB each, sharing a valid 1 MiB physical range and a matching u32 ccp_text, pass monotonic coverage and physical bounds. The loop attempts about 4.29 billion StoryChar records (at least tens of GiB), before package admission.

findings.summary: The independent preindex footer parser can count a different EOCD or count field from zip 9.0.5. Neither admission nor PartFs enforces the actual opened count; duplicate detection also trusts the unrelated declared count.
